Hi Alex — great to hear from you and glad the latency looked reasonable. Short answers up front: yes, you can start on Hosted for the pilot and toggle up to a small Dedicated pool later; and we can enable select premium features for pilot customers without full enterprise licensing.

Notes:
- Hosted + aggressive batching is lower friction and lower upfront cost; good for validating quality and integration.
- Dedicated gives predictable tail latency and isolated resources for production but requires a small minimum commit.
- We offer a pilot bundle that includes a one-time onboarding credit and a pilot discount for the first 3 months (typically 15–25% depending on committed monthly spend).

I'll loop in our pricing lead to propose a compact set of packaging options and a short spreadsheet with numbers. Would you prefer a turnkey small Dedicated pool estimate or a Hosted-first plan with burst to Dedicated?

Best,
Chloe Martin

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Fwd: Quick question — packaging for a 6-mo pilot

Chloe — below are three distinct, customer-friendly packaging options. I attached pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx with line-item math.

Option A — Hosted-first pilot (lowest friction)- What: Hosted API only; aggressive batching and prefix caching; enable KV caching and 8-bit quant profiles per-call; metered billing.
- Pros: No minimum commit; fastest onboarding; low upfront cost. Good to validate model quality.
- Cons: Variable cost; potential tail latency variability for charting calls; we recommend client-side small retry/backoff.
- Pricing/discount: metered spend estimate $6k–$9k/mo, offer 20% discount for first 3 months + $4k onboarding credit.

Option B — Hybrid pilot (recommended for them)- What: Hosted for bulk nightly batch, small Dedicated pool (1-2 GPU equivalent reserved) for low-latency charting calls; KV caching + custom quant profiles enabled on Dedicated.
- Pros: Predictable charting latency (<500ms median), lower per-token cost on Dedicated for critical routes, clear separation of batch vs interactive.
- Cons: Small commit required (monthly reserved capacity).
- Pricing/discount: Dedicated reserve ~$8k/mo + Hosted metered ~$2k/mo; offer a 25% pilot discount on Dedicated for first 3 months + $6k onboarding credit.

Option C — Short-term Dedicated trial- What: Temporary Dedicated pool (90-day minimum) with elevated SLA and included feature toggles.
- Pros: Production-like environment, best latency guarantees.
- Cons: Highest upfront; procurement friction.
- Pricing/discount: Reserve ~$12k/mo; pilot pricing can be 30% off first 90 days if they sign a 6-month commitment; includes 1-day priority onboarding.

Additional notes / tradeoffs:
- Feature gating: We can enable KV-prefix caching + custom quant profiles for pilots; any kernel-level optimizations that require image changes are scoped and may take extra time.
- Rollout/fallback: Recommend hybrid approach so batch runs on Hosted (cheaper) and critical interactive routes go to Dedicated — we can route by API key/route.
- Credits/discount mechanics: Apply pilot discount on invoices; onboarding credit is a one-time invoice credit applied after first invoice.

Proposal: Lead with Option B (Hybrid) — it balances procurement risk and performance. Offer 25% off Dedicated for the first 3 months + $6k credit; include an SLA exception for pilot (24/7 support for critical incidents) in the SOW.

If that sounds good, we can turn this into a short SOW and draft an invoice for procurement.

— Lauren
Director, Enterprise Pricing
